back: Accurate titres that agree within 0.10 cm³; the mean titre is calculated from these only.
To the nearest 0.05 cm³, two decimal places (e.g. 23.45 cm³). Uncertainty of a titre ±0.10 cm³ (two readings).
uncertainty ÷ measured value × 100; for a difference of two readings, use twice the reading uncertainty.
An error that shifts every reading the same way (e.g. heat loss, an uncalibrated balance). Not reduced by repeating; fix the method.
Unpredictable scatter either side of the true value (e.g. judging an end point). Reduced by repeating and averaging.
Heat, cool, weigh and repeat until two consecutive masses agree (e.g. within 0.01 g): shows the reaction or water loss is complete.

front: Significant figures in a calculated answer
back: The same as the least precise data, or one more. Round only the final answer.

front: Correcting ΔT in a thermometric experiment
back: Extrapolate the before-mixing line forward and the cooling line back to the time of mixing; ΔT is the vertical gap between them.
Quantity / unit, e.g. 'titre / cm³', 'temperature / °C'; every value in a column to the same number of decimal places.
